FARRA:v2p196/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p196/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p196/r6.claim: من in both clauses is nominative; this is the pattern when a Quranic من follows a raising verb, though accusative is also possible as in الله يعلم المفسد من المصلح.
FARRA:v2p196/r6.anchor: وكل ما كان في القرآن مثله فهو مرفوع إذا كان بعده رافع

STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r2.claim: The surah followed Maryam and figures in ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb’s conversion account: after reading its parchment at his sister’s house, he resolved to become Muslim and went to profess faith to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r2.anchor: resolved to become Muslim, and went to

STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r4.claim: The surah consoles the Prophet, recounts Moses and Adam, addresses the Last Day, urges steadfastness amid Makkan insults, and closes by warning the Makkans of the inevitable end.
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r4.anchor: The sūrah begins with a consolation to the Prophet and speaks of God’s all-encompassing knowledge and His Most Beautiful Names

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.claim: The surah closes with encouragement for the Prophet and believers facing pressure: punishment awaits its divinely set time, so believers should endure, worship steadily, and keep striving; this work benefits them, and a blessed future belongs to the God-conscious.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.anchor: müminlerin İslâm mesajının hedefine ulaşması için bu tür beklentilere bel bağlamak yerine karşılaştıkları zorluklara katlanmaları, sürekli bir ibadet bilinci ve disiplini içinde mücadeleye devam etmeleri istenmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r10.claim: After the message is properly delivered, those who persist in their assumptions are left to the freedom of choice granted in worldly life, though they will eventually see the truth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r10.anchor: dünya hayatında insana verilen seçim özgürlüğünün bir sonucu olarak bu kuruntularıyla baş başa bırakılmalıdırlar, ama bir gün gerçekleri bütün çıplaklığıyla görüp anlayacaklardır.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r2.claim: After Moses' account, the concluding verses address Muhammad and return to the surah's opening theme.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r2.anchor: sūrah ends on the topic with which it began

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r3.claim: The Prophet must await God's decision patiently; haste gives Satan an opening, as Adam's haste led to his deception, and prayer helps secure patience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r3.anchor: It was because of hastiness that Adam (sws) was deceived by Satan.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r4.claim: He should not pursue the wealthy to bolster his ranks because God provides his preaching's resources and financial needs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r4.anchor: His preaching has its own resources and God has taken upon Himself to fulfil his financial needs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p5/r5.claim: Those demanding punishment should be told that the Prophet's duty was to warn; he too awaits the punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r2.claim: The final section resumes the introductory theme and addresses the Prophet: opponents who lead others astray carry both their own sins and those of their followers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r2.anchor: will not only bear their own burden of sins on the Day of Judgement but also of those who were led astray by them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r3.claim: The Prophet should recite the comprehensive warning to all; willing hearers benefit, evasive people are left alone, and he is not accountable for them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r3.anchor: he who evades it should be left alone by him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r3.claim: Those demanding a sign of the promised doom should wait, as the Prophet is told to wait too.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r3.anchor: if they think that this sign is not enough and would like a sign of the promised doom, then they should wait and he too will wait

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p89/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p89/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p89/r1.claim: The final warning shifts from the indirect address of the preceding two verses to direct address, signaling the intensity of anger; a parallel clause is omitted because contextual indications make it clear.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p89/r1.anchor: In this verse, the address has become direct to express the intensity of anger.

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r1.claim: متربص is the predicate of كل and is singular because it agrees with the word form of كل.

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r2.claim: The clearer parse makes من interrogative and initial, with أصحاب as its predicate; the clause fills the two object positions of تعلمون.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r2.anchor: أظهرهما: أن تكون استفهامية مبتدأة، و " أصحاب " خبره. والجملة في محل نصب سادة

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r3.claim: Al-Farra instead takes من as a relative pronoun and أصحاب as the predicate of an omitted هم; this follows their allowance of a deleted resumptive even in a short relative clause.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r3.anchor: ويعزى للفراء أن تكون موصولة بمعنى الذين. و " أصحاب " خبر مبتدأ مضمر

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r4.claim: علم may mean know by recognition and take this one object, or retain its usual sense and require an implied second object.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r4.anchor: ثم " علم " يجوز أن تكون عرفانية فتكتفي بهذا المفعول، وأن تكون على بابها

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r5.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r5.claim: The general reading is السوي, on the pattern فعيل, meaning straight or level.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r5.anchor: وقرأ العامة: " السوي " على وزن فعيل بمعنى المستوي.

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r6.speaker: أبو مجلز وعمران بن حدير
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r6.claim: Abu Majliz and Imran ibn Hudayr read السواء with fatḥa and a long vowel, meaning the good middle course.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز وعمران بن حدير " السواء " بفتح السين والمد، بمعنى الوسط الجيد.

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r7.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر والجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r7.claim: Yahya ibn Yamar and al-Jahdari read السوءى on the feminine فعلى pattern, since الصراط can be masculine or feminine.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r7.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر والجحدري " السوءى " على فعلى باعتبار أن الصراط يذكر ويؤنث.

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reads السوء with an open sīn, meaning evil.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس " السوء " بفتح السين بمعنى الشر.

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r9.claim: A doubled-wāw form with ḍamma on the sīn may reflect replacement of hamza by wāw followed by assimilation.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r9.anchor: وروي عنهما " السوى " بضم السين وتشديد الواو. ويحتمل ذلك وجهين، أحدهما: أن

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r10.claim: The same doubled-wāw form could be the feminine of سواء; changing yā to wāw reverses the expected change when a quiescent yā and wāw meet.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r10.anchor: وأن يكون فعلى من السواء. وأصله السويا فقلبت الياء واوا وأدغم أيضا.

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats a reading with ḍamma on sīn and doubled yā as a diminutive of سوء; the Shaykh objects that this should retain the hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r11.anchor: تصغير " سوء " قاله الزمخشري. قال الشيخ: " وليس بجيد إذ لو كان كذلك لثبتت همزة

SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r12.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r12.claim: The Shaykh prefers deriving that diminutive reading from سواء, as عطي is used for عطاء; Abu al-Baqa also derives it from سوء, and the author notes that replacing this hamza is permissible.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135/r12.anchor: كقولهم عطي في عطاء ". قلت: وقد جعله أبو البقاء أيضا تصغير السوء

SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r1.claim: One parse makes من interrogative, following the same syntax as the earlier من, except that the resumptive pronoun is omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r1.anchor: أحدها: أن تكون استفهامية، وحكمها كالتي قبلها إلا في حذف العائد.

SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r2.claim: A second parse makes من a relative pronoun in the nominative, on the previously described analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنها في محل رفع على ما تقدم في الاستفهامية.

SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r3.claim: A third parse makes the relative pronoun genitive by coordination with الصراط, meaning the people who followed guidance.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r3.anchor: في محل جر نسقا على " الصراط " أي: وأصحاب من اهتدى.

SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the second parse coordinates a declarative predicate with an interrogative, supporting al-Farra's relative-pronoun analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:20:135#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو البقاء في الوجه الثاني: " وفيه عطف الخبر على الاستفهام، وفيه تقوية قول الفراء "

ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r1.claim: من is nominative and is not governed by فستعلمون, whose meaning is an equivalence question: which of us or them follows the straight path?
ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r1.anchor: في موضع رفع، ولا يجوز أن يعمل فيها (فستعلمون)، لأن معناه معنى التسوية،

ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r2.claim: أصحاب الصراط السوي means people of the upright path; an alternative construal contrasts people of the worse path with the one rightly guided.
ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r2.anchor: ومعنى (أصحاب الصراط السوي) أصحاب الطريق المستقيم، ويجوز من أصحاب الصراط السوي ومن اهتدى.

ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r3.claim: The alternative explanation asks which people belong to the worse way and which person is guided.
ZAJJAJ:v3p381/r3.anchor: أي فسيعلمون من أصحاب الطريقة السوءى ومن المهتدي.

ASAD-NOTES:20:135/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:135/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:135/r1.claim: All are waiting for the future; the Judgment will reveal who followed the even path and who found guidance.
ASAD-NOTES:20:135/r1.anchor: waiting [for what the future may bring]: [122] wait, then, [for the Day of Judgment - ]

ASAD-NOTES:20:135#n122/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:135#n122/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:135#n122/r1.claim: Everyone, whatever their beliefs or circumstances, hopes that their chosen way of life will prove right.
ASAD-NOTES:20:135#n122/r1.anchor: no man, whatever his persuasion or condition, can ever cease to hope that the way of life chosen by him

QIRAAT-ER:20:135:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:135:10#1/r1.speaker: ibdāl|sp
QIRAAT-ER:20:135:10#1/r1.claim: The sīn reading is dialectal and canonical; the source calls sīn etymologically original and ṣād the emphatic Qurayshī adaptation.
QIRAAT-ER:20:135:10#1/r1.anchor: ibdāl|sp, mutawatir: Sīn replaces ṣād — dialectal variant; both canonical; sīn is the etymological original

QIRAAT-ER:20:135:10#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:135:10#2/r1.speaker: ibdāl
QIRAAT-ER:20:135:10#2/r1.claim: Ishmām blends ṣād slightly toward zāy, yielding an intermediate sound between ṣād and sīn.
QIRAAT-ER:20:135:10#2/r1.anchor: ibdāl, mutawatir: Ṣād with ishmām (slight blending toward zāy) — intermediate pronunciation between ṣād and sīn

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r1.claim: Each side waits for the outcome; this threatens and warns the disbelievers, and the singular predicate follows كل’s grammatical form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r1.anchor: قل كل متربص فتربصوا أي منتظر منا ومنكم عاقبة أمره، وفي ذلك تهديد لهم ووعيد وأفرد الخبر وهو متربص حملا على لفظ كل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r2.claim: من أصحاب is a subject and predicate; فستعلمون is suspended from governing it because the clause is interrogative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r2.anchor: ومن أصحاب مبتدأ وخبر علق عنه فستعلمون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ allows من as a relative pronoun and object of فستعلمون, with أصحاب as predicate of an omitted subject; this follows the Kufan allowance for deleting the relative-clause pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r3.anchor: وأجاز الفراء أن تكون ما موصولة بمعنى الذي فتكون مفعولة بفستعلمون وأصحاب خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r4.claim: The majority read السوي as ṣawiyy, meaning straight or even.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور السوي على وزن فعيل أي المستوي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r5.speaker: أبو مجلز، عمران بن حدير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r5.claim: Abu Mujliz and Imran ibn Hudayr read السواء, meaning the middle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز وعمران بن حدير السواء أي الوسط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r6.speaker: الجحدري، ابن يعمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r6.claim: Al-Jahdari and Ibn Yaʿmar read السوأى, a feminine form treated as opposite to guidance and contrasted with ومن اهتدى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وابن يعمر السوأى على وزن فعلى أنث لتأنيث الصراط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to read الصراط السوء; the transmitted السوأى may derive either from السووى with hamza changed to wāw or from السواء with yā changed to wāw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r7.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك قراءة ابن عباس الصراط السوء وقد روي عنهما أنهما قرآ السوأى على وزن فعلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls the reading with ḍamma on sīn a diminutive of سوء; Abu Hayyan rejects this because the hamza should remain, preferring a diminutive of سواء like عطاء to عطي.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r8.anchor: وقرىء السوي بضم السين وفتح الواو وشد الياء تصغير السوء. قاله الزمخشري، وليس بجيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r9.claim: Reading السوأى or السوء makes the contrast with guidance explicit, unlike the majority reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p402/r9.anchor: ومن قرأ السوأى أو السوء كان في ذلك مقابلة لقوله ومن اهتدى وعلى قراءة الجمهور لم تراع المقابلة في الاستفهام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r1.claim: Each side, believers and disbelievers, awaits the outcome of its affair; mutarabbis is the predicate of kull and is singular to match kull’s grammatical form.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r1.anchor: أي منتظر لما يؤل اليه أمرنا وأمركم وهو خبر كل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r2.claim: A variant reading has fa-tamattaʿū in place of fa-tarabbaṣū.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r3.claim: Al-sawī means straight; the promised outcome will show who possesses the straight path and who is guided from error.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r3.anchor: أي المستقيم وقرأ أبو مجلز وعمران بن حدير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r4.speaker: أبو مجلز وعمران بن حدير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r4.claim: Abu Mujliz and Imran ibn Hudayr read al-siwāʾ, meaning the middle or excellent path.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو مجلز وعمران بن حدير ( السواء ) أي الوسط

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r5.speaker: الجحدري وابن يعمر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r5.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī and Ibn Yaʿmar read al-sūʾā, a feminine form of al-aswaʾ, with feminine agreement because ṣirāṭ may be feminine.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r5.anchor: بالضم والقصر على وزن فعلى وهو تأنيث الاسوا وأنث لتأنيث

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reads al-sūʾ, meaning evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r6.anchor: رضى الله تعالى عنهما ( السوء ) بفتح وسكون وهمزة آخره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r7.claim: For the variant al-suyy with doubled yāʾ, Abu Hayyan prefers deriving it as a diminutive of sawāʾ, like ʿaṭā becoming ʿaṭiyy, because a diminutive of the proposed form should retain its hamza.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الاجود أن يكون تصغير سواء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r8.claim: The author reports the objection that exchanging the hamza for yāʾ is permissible, and another al-suyy reading with doubled wāw is explained as a softened al-sūʾā.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r8.anchor: وتعقب بأن إبدال مثل هذه الهمزة ياء جائز

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r9.claim: Wa-man ihtadā means whoever was guided out of error; the comparison implicit in this wording is absent in the majority reading and in the first anomalous reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r9.anchor: أي من الضلالة ولم تراع على قراءة الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r10.claim: On the main parsing, both man clauses are interrogative subjects with following predicates; together they fill the suspended verb’s two objects, or its one object if ʿalima means to know.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r10.anchor: ومن في الموضعين استفهامية في محل رفع على الأبتداء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r11.claim: A second man may be relative and coordinate with the first interrogative clause if ʿalima means to know; otherwise coordination would leave an impermissibly omitted object.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r11.anchor: وجوز كون من الثانية موصولة فتكون معطوفة على محل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r12.claim: Alternatively, the second clause can coordinate with aṣḥāb or ṣirāṭ, asking who is guided or who belongs to the guided one’s path; if both refer to the Prophet, the coordination joins descriptions of one person.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r12.anchor: فتكون في حيز من الاستفهامية أي ومن الذي اهتدى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r13.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r13.claim: Al-Farrāʾ permits the first man to be a relative pronoun functioning as the object of ʿilm, with aṣḥāb as the predicate of an elided subject; Kūfans allow omission of this relative pronoun, unlike Basrans.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r13.anchor: وأجاز الفراء أن تكون من الأولى موصولة أيضا بمعنى الذين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r14.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r14.claim: Al-Tibi sees the ending as answering the opening: after bearing the burden of proclamation without exhausting oneself, the Prophet should worship within his capacity and leave those whom warning will not benefit; they will regret their opposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287/r14.anchor: وما أشد مناسبة هذه الخاتمة للفاتحة وقد ذكر الطيبي انها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p289#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289#2/r6.claim: The connection of Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ to the preceding sūra is self-evident.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289#2/r6.anchor: ووجه اتصالهما بما قبلهما غني عن البيان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p305/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p305/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p305/r1.claim: The polytheists said they were waiting for time’s reversals, hoping Muhammad would die so they could be rid of him; God tells them to wait.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p305/r1.anchor: منتظر دوائر الزمان، وذلك أن المشركين قالوا نتربص بمحمد حوادث الدهر، فإذا مات تخلصنا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p305/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p305/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p305/r2.claim: When God’s command arrives and the Resurrection begins, it will become clear who is on the upright path and rightly guided, the believers or their opponents.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p305/r2.anchor: فانتظروا، {فستعلمون} إذا جاء أمر الله وقامت القيامة، {من أصحاب الصراط السوي}

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r4.claim: Each side is waiting to see what its affair will come to.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r5.claim: Another reading is fa-tamattaʿū, so enjoy yourselves.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r5.anchor: منتظر لما يؤول إليه أمرنا وأمركم. { فتربصوا } وقرىء «فتمتعوا».

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r6.claim: Al-ṣirāṭ al-sawī is the straight path.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r7.claim: Reported readings include al-sawāʾ, the good middle; al-sūʾ, evil; and al-suwayy, a diminutive of al-sūʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r7.anchor: وقرىء «السواء» أي الوسط الجيد و «السوآى» و «السوء» أي الشر، و «السوي» هو تصغيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r8.claim: Both instances of man may be interrogative nominative subjects; the second may instead be relative, coordinated with the suspended interrogative clause, its subject, or the path if that means the Prophet.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الثانية موصولة بخلاف الأولى لعدم العائد فتكون معطوفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:134-135/r9.claim: A report from the Prophet promises the reader of Ṭā Hā the reward of the Emigrants and Helpers on Judgment Day.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r4.claim: Their faith is nearly impossible and their disputation will not end: they criticize guidance if it comes and protest if punishment comes, so the Prophet is told that both sides await the outcome.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r4.anchor: وجدالهم لا ينقطع , بل إن جاءهم الهدى طعنوا فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r5.claim: The ṣirāṭ is a clear, broad road; sawiyy means straight, without a bend or rise, and fit to reach one's aims.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r5.anchor: أي الذي لا عوج فيه ولا نتو

BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r6.claim: Possessing something does not mean one knows or uses it, so the verse also asks who attained guidance, gained benefit, and avoided harm: the Prophet's side or theirs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r6.anchor: قد لا يكون عالما بالشيء ولا عاملا بما يعلم منه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r7.claim: The outcome became clear at the conquest of Mecca: they rejoiced greatly in Islam and entered it from hope in clemency and generosity and fear of the sword and punishment, later marveling at their earlier hesitation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r7.anchor: ودخلوا رغبة في الحلم والكرم , ورهبة من السيف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r8.claim: The Prophet and his followers are the fortunate, content people in both lives; the end of the sūrah returns to its opening assurance that revelation was not sent to make the Prophet miserable, showing God's forbearance toward the exalted.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p61/r8.anchor: هم السعداء الأغنياء الراضون في الدنيا والآخرة

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r1.claim: Each of the two sides, the Prophet's party and the opponents, waits for the outcome of their affairs.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r1.anchor: انتظار الأمر أو زواله منتظرا لما يؤول إليه أمرنا وأمركم.

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r2.claim: Kashifi glosses this as the opponents waiting for the Prophet's misfortune while the believers await their punishment.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r2.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يعني شما نكبت ما راشم ميداريد وما عقوبت شمارا).

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r3.speaker: الكبير
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r3.claim: Al-Kabir says each side awaits the outcome before death through jihad and the rise of power, or after death through reward and punishment, with honor for the truthful and humiliation for the false.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r3.anchor: قال في "الكبير" : كل منا ومنكم منتظر عاقبة أمره إما قبل الموت بسبب الجهاد

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r4.claim: The polytheists said they would wait for time's events until Muhammad died and they were rid of him; God answers that they should wait.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r4.anchor: وروي أن المشركين قالوا : نتربص بمحمد حوادث الدهر فإذا مات تخلصنا فقال تعالى : {فتربصوا}

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r5.claim: When God's command arrives soon, the parties will learn which of them follows the straight path.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r5.anchor: عن قريب إذا جاء أمر الله

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r6.claim: A straight path is a way without bends or deviation, following a balanced course.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r6.anchor: والصراط من السبيل ما لا التواء فيه أي : لا إعوجاج بل يكون على سبيل القصد

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r7.claim: The question asks which side escaped misguidance: the Prophet's side or theirs.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r7.anchor: من الضلال أي : أنحن أم أنتم

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r8.claim: A verse of poetry pictures the eventual exposure of the truth: when the dust clears, one will see whether a horseman or a donkey is beneath him.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r8.anchor: كما قال بعضهم : سوف ترى إذا انجلى الغبار أفرس تحتك أم حمار

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r9.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r9.claim: Kashifi identifies the Prophet as the one intended: he is both guided and a guide to others.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r9.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (مراد حضرت يغمبرست كه هم راه يافته وهم راه نماينده است)

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r10.claim: In the inward reading, the guided reach God by traversing the spiritual stations and detaching from all besides Him; the others cut themselves off by attaching to something else.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r10.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى المهتدين بالوصول إليه بقطع المنازل والانفصال عما سواه والمنقطعين عنه باتصال غيره

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r11.speaker: الخجندي
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r11.claim: Khujandi's couplet says union is attained only by severance, beginning with separation from all else.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r11.anchor: كما قال الخجندي : وصل ميسر نشود جز بقطع

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r12.claim: God has removed excuses by granting respite and guidance; the decisive proof belongs to God.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r12.anchor: واعلم أن الله تعالى قطع المعذرة بالإمهال و"الإرشاد" فلله الحجة البالغة

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r13.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r13.claim: A Prophetic report names three who plead excuses before God: one who died in the interval, someone without reason, and a child; they are tested with a fire, and their response reveals their standing.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r13.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال : قال عليه السلام : "يحتج على الله ثلاثة

BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r14.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r14.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports that the people of Paradise recite no Qur'an except Surat Ta Ha and Ya Sin.
BURSEVI:v5p345#3/r14.anchor: وفي الحديث : "لا يقرأ أهل الجنة من القرآن إلا سورة طه ويس"

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.claim: The ending closes the debate and echoes the opening: the Prophet has delivered guidance, so he may take comfort in completing his mission while the heedless remain astray until truth becomes clear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.anchor: وهي قوله { ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى } ( طه : 2 )

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r6.claim: God instructs the Prophet to warn them and to have both sides wait for relief and the outcome.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r6.anchor: ثم أمر الله تعالى نبيه أن يتوعدهم ويحملهم ونفسه على التربص وانتظار الفرج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r7.claim: Tarabbus means waiting deliberately; ṣirāṭ means a road.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r8.claim: One group reads al-sawiyy and another al-sūʾ, a difference that divides the two parties into contrasting outcomes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r8.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «السوي» ، وقرأت فرقة «السوء» فكأن هذه القراءة قسمت الفريقين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r9.claim: Other reported forms include al-sawiyy with a doubled, open wāw and al-sūʾā with a ḍamma and hamza on the wāw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r9.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «السوي» بشد الواو وفتحها، وقرأت فرقة «السوؤى» بضم السين وهمزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r10.claim: The verb for being guided means to be rightly directed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71#2/r10.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «السوؤى» بضم السين وهمزة على الواو على وزن فعلى، واهتدى معناه رشد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r1.claim: Each side is waiting: Muhammad and the believers await the unbelievers' punishment in this life, while the unbelievers await calamities for them; then each is told to wait.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r1.anchor: كل منا ومنكم متربص أي نحن نتربص بكم العذاب في الدنيا وأنتم تتربصون بنا الدوائر فتربصوا أي فانتظروا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r2.claim: The straight path is the upright religion, and “who is guided” means guided away from error; the rhetorical question asks which side is guided, us or them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r2.anchor: من اصحاب الصراط السوي أي الدين المستقيم ومن اهتدى من الضلالة أنحن أم أنتم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r3.claim: An unnamed view says this verse was abrogated by the sword verse, conventionally 9:5; Ibn al-Jawzi rejects that claim as baseless.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p337/r3.anchor: وقيل هذه منسوخة بآية السيف وليس بشيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to say that both sides, the believers and the deniers, are waiting, so they should wait for the outcome.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r2.claim: The sound path is the straight road; the guided person is one who reached truth and the way of right direction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r2.anchor: أي: الطريق المستقيم، {ومن اهتدى} إلى الحق وسبيل الرشاد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r3.claim: The warning resembles 25:42, where they will learn who is farther astray, and 54:26, which says they will know who is the great liar.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p330/r3.anchor: وهذا كقوله (1) تعالى {وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا}

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r1.claim: Both sides await the outcome of their respective affairs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r1.anchor: أي كل واحد منا ومنكم { متربص } للعاقبة ولما يؤول إليه أمرنا وأمركم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r2.claim: Al-sawāʾ is read as middle or best, even or upright, and with related forms glossed as diminutives of al-sūʾ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r2.anchor: وقرىء : ( السواء ) بمعنى الوسط والجيد . أو المستوى والسوء والسوأي والسوي تصغير السوء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r3.speaker: أبو رافع
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r3.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ says he memorized from the Prophet the variant ‘Enjoy yourselves; soon you will know.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r3.anchor: وقرىء : ( فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون ) قال أبو رافع : حفظته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r4.claim: A report promises a reciter of Ṭā-Hā the Resurrection reward of the Emigrants and Helpers; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r4.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r5.claim: A second report says Paradise’s people recite no Qur’an except Ṭā-Hā and Yā-Sīn; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p100/r5.anchor: وقال : ( 690 ) ( لا يقرأ أهل الجنة من القرآن إلا طه ويس )

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r1.claim: “Each waiting” means that each party is waiting.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r2.claim: Each party may be waiting to gain victory over its opponent.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r3.claim: Alternatively, each awaits the outcome that will make the truth of its conduct manifest.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r4.claim: The command to wait is a threat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r4.anchor: { فتربصوا } وهذا تهديد . { فستعلمون من أصحاب

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r5.claim: Victory will reveal who is best guided to the true religion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r5.anchor: فستعلمون بالنصر من أهدى إلى دين الحق

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r6.claim: Alternatively, on Judgment Day they will learn who was guided to the path of Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p434/r6.anchor: فستعلمون يوم القيامة من أهدى إلى طريق الجنة

MUQATIL:20:133-135/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r5.claim: Meccan unbelievers awaited Muhammad's death, while Muhammad awaited the worldly punishment he had threatened them with.
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r5.anchor: كفار مكة، قالوا: نتربص بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، الموت لأن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم، أوعدهم العذاب فى الدنيا

MUQATIL:20:133-135/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r6.claim: God commands the Meccans to wait as they do, while Muhammad waits for their worldly punishment to descend.
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r6.anchor: { قل } لكفار مكة { كل متربص } أنتم بمحمد الموت، ومحمد يتربص بكم العذاب فى الدنيا

MUQATIL:20:133-135/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r7.claim: The straight path is justice; the question is which side, us or you, is rightly guided.
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r7.anchor: من أصحاب الصراط السوى } يعني العدل أنحن أم أنتم { ومن اهتدى } [آية: 135] منا ومنكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r1.claim: Each side—Messenger and opponents—is awaiting what its outcome will be.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ قل كل ﴾ أي كل واحد منا ومنكم ﴿ متربص ﴾ منتظر للعقابة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r2.claim: The command to wait is addressed to the opponents.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ متربص ﴾ منتظر للعقابة ولما يؤل اليه أمرنا وامركم ﴿ فتربصوا ﴾ أنتم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r3.claim: At the Resurrection they will learn who follows the sound path and is guided to everlasting bliss.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ فستعلمون ﴾ إذا جاءت القيامة ﴿ من أصحاب ﴾ مبتدا وخبر ومحلهما نصب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r4.claim: The two clauses “who are the people of the path” and “who is guided” are subjects with predicates, and together occupy the accusative position.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r4.anchor: ﴿ من أصحاب ﴾ مبتدا وخبر ومحلهما نصب ﴿ الصراط السوي ﴾ المستقيم ﴿ ومن اهتدى ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r5.speaker: رسول الله
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r5.claim: A report from the Messenger says that the people of Paradise recite only Sūrat Ṭā Hā and Yā Sīn; no grading is given.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73#3/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يقرأ أهل الجنة إلى سورة طه ويس

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r6.claim: Muhammad is told to say that believers and unbelievers alike await what time will bring and which side will win.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r6.anchor: أي قل لهم يا محمد كل متربص، أي كل المؤمنين والكافرين منتظر دوائر الزمان ولمن يكون النصر.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r7.claim: The level path is the upright religion and guidance; victory will show who follows the true religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r7.anchor: يريد الدين المستقيم والهدى والمعنى: فستعلمون بالنصر من اهتدى إلى دين الحق.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r8.claim: Another view places the recognition on Judgment Day, when people will know who was guided to the path of Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r8.anchor: وقيل: فستعلمون يوم القيامة من اهتدى إلى طريق الجنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r9.claim: The verse closes the sūra with a threat, warning, and intimidation.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r9.anchor: وفي هذا ضرب من الوعيد والتخويف والتهديد ختم به السورة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r10.speaker: أبو رافع
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r10.claim: A reading has فسوف تعلمون; Abu Rafiʿ says he memorized it from the Prophet, as cited by al-Zamakhshari.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r10.anchor: وقرىء «فسوف تعلمون». قال أبو رافع: حفظته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكره الزمخشري.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r11.speaker: الزجاج والفراء وأبو إسحاق والنحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses من as nominative; al-Farraʾ allows accusative like 2:220. Abu Ishaq objects that an interrogative cannot be governed by what precedes and parses it as an initial subject: are we or you on the straight path?
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r11.anchor: و«من» في موضع رفع عند الزجاج. وقال الفراء: يجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب مثل والله يعلم المفسد من المصلح

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r12.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r12.claim: Al-Nahhas explains al-Farraʾ's sense as asking who did not stray and who strayed before becoming guided.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r12.anchor: قال النحاس: والفراء يذهب إلى أن معنى { من أصحاب الصراط السوي } من لم يضل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r13.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r13.claim: Yahya ibn Yaʿmar and ʿAsim al-Jahdari read السوا with a doubled wāw and feminine alif, on fuʿla; making الصراط feminine is rare, whereas 1:6 uses the masculine.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r13.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري «فسيعلمون من أصحاب الصراط السوا» بتشديد الواو بعدها ألف التأنيث

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r14.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r14.claim: Abu Hatim rejects السوا: from سوء it should be السوءى, and from سواء it should be السيا with kasra.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r14.anchor: وقد رد هذا أبو حاتم قال: إن كان من السوء وجب أن يقال السوءى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the reading السواء can mean the middle, justice, or what is straight.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r15.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وقرىء «السواء» بمعنى الوسط والعدل أو المستوي.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r16.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r16.claim: Al-Nahhas allows the reading by positing original السوءى, with the hamza replaced by wāw after a preceding ḍamma.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:134-135/r16.anchor: النحاس: وجواز قراءة يحيى بن يعمر والجحدري أن يكون الأصل «السوءى»

RAZI-FULL:v22p119/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p119/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p119/r4.claim: Each side, the believers and their opponents, awaits the outcome of its affair; this waiting may occur before death, at death, or after death when reward and punishment distinguish the vindicated from the false.
RAZI-FULL:v22p119/r4.anchor: أي كل منا ومنكم منتظر عاقبة أمره وهذا الانتظار يحتمل أن يكون قبل الموت

RAZI-FULL:v22p119/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p119/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p119/r5.claim: The promise that they will know who follows the straight path is a threat and rebuke to unbelievers, not an expression of doubt.
RAZI-FULL:v22p119/r5.anchor: وليس هو بمعنى الشك والترديد ، بل هو على سبيل التهديد والزجر للكفار

STUDYQURAN:20:135/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:135/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:135/r1.claim: Each party waits to see its outcome, either in this life or at death.
STUDYQURAN:20:135/r1.anchor: That each is waiting means each party is waiting to see what its outcome will be, either in this life or at the time of death

STUDYQURAN:20:135/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:135/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:135/r2.claim: The promise that they will come to know is meant to threaten and frighten the disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:20:135/r2.anchor: The words for you shall come to know are intended to threaten and frighten the disbelievers

TAB-FULL:v16p220/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p220/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p220/r1.claim: Both sides wait to see who will prevail; when God's command comes and the Resurrection is established, they will learn who followed the straight path and was guided.
TAB-FULL:v16p220/r1.anchor: فستعلمون من أهل الطريق المستقيم المعتدل الذي لا اعوجاج فيه إذا جاء أمر الله وقامت القيامة، أنحن أم أنتم؟

TAB-FULL:v16p220/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p220/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p220/r2.claim: At that time it will be clear whether the two sides or their opponents follow the straight, moderate path without deviation and are truly guided.
TAB-FULL:v16p220/r2.anchor: فستعلمون من أهل الطريق المستقيم المعتدل الذي لا اعوجاج فيه إذا جاء أمر الله وقامت القيامة، أنحن أم أنتم؟

TAB-FULL:v16p220/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p220/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p220/r3.claim: Both occurrences of من may be nominative with تعلمون left ungoverned, as in the cave-companions verse, or accusative under تعلمون, as in the verse distinguishing corrupter from reformer.
TAB-FULL:v16p220/r3.anchor: وفي «من» من قوله: {فستعلمون من أصحاب الصراط السوي} [طه: 135] والثانية من قوله: {ومن اهتدى} [طه: 135] وجهان: الرفع، وترك أعمال تعلمون فيهما

TABATABAI:20:134-135/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:134-135/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:134-135/r3.claim: Tarabbus means waiting, and the straight path is the upright road; each side waits for its desired outcome and follows a way toward it.
TABATABAI:20:134-135/r3.anchor: التربص الانتظار، والصراط السوي الطريق المستقيم،

TABATABAI:20:134-135/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:134-135/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:134-135/r4.claim: The believers await God’s promised triumph, the advance of His religion, and the completion of His light; the opponents await reversals that would extinguish the true call.
TABATABAI:20:134-135/r4.anchor: فنحن ننتظر ما وعده الله لنا فيكم وفي تقدم دينه وتمام نوره

TABATABAI:20:134-135/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:134-135/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:134-135/r5.claim: The command to wait is a threat: the parties will learn which follows the straight road to its goal and is guided; the verse foretells a victory.
TABATABAI:20:134-135/r5.anchor: وفيه تهديد فستعلمون أي طائفة منا ومنكم أصحاب الطريق المستقيم

FARRA:v2p197/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p197/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p197/r1.claim: The straight path belongs to those who did not go astray; “who is guided” refers to those who had been astray and then found guidance.
FARRA:v2p197/r1.anchor: الذين لم يضلوا (ومن اهتدى) ممن كان ضالا فهدى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p565#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p565#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p565#2/r1.claim: “Each” means both sides: the Muslims wait for God's promise concerning the opponents, while the opponents await calamity that would let them be rid of the Muslims; “wait” means await.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p565#2/r1.anchor: منكم {متربص} مهو نحن نتربص بكم وعدا لنا فيكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p565#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p565#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p565#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the even path as the upright religion.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p565#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p565#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p565#2/r3.claim: The question is which of the two sides is guided away from error: “we or you?”

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:135/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:135/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:135/r1.claim: Muhammad is to tell both sides that each awaits how events turn and which side wins; at the Resurrection they will know who follows the straight path, the Muslims or their opponents.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:135/r1.anchor: منتظر دوائر الزمان، ولمن يكون النصر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r6.claim: The command is for the Prophet to say that both sides are waiting.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r6.anchor: قال الله تبارك وتعالى للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: {قل كل متربص} [طه: 135] نحن وأنتم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r7.claim: The polytheists waited for the Prophet to die, while the Prophet waited for punishment to come upon them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r7.anchor: وكان المشركون يتربصون بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يموت، وكان النبي عليه السلام يتربص بهم أن يجيئهم العذاب

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r8.claim: The even, upright path is the just straight road to Paradise.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r9.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r9.claim: Al-Suddi explains the even path as the just religion, Islam.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r9.anchor: وقال السدي: {الصراط السوي} [طه: 135] يعني: الدين العدل، وهو الإسلام.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p296/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p296/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p296/r1.claim: It will become clear that the Prophet and believers followed the upright road to Paradise and died guided.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p296/r1.anchor: فستعلمون أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين كانوا على الصراط السوي، وهو طريق الجنة

NAHHAS:v3p61/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p61/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p61/r4.claim: من is nominative in the question about who follows the straight path.
NAHHAS:v3p61/r4.anchor: من في موضع رفع وقال الفراء يجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب

NAHHAS:v3p61/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p61/r5.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p61/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows من to be accusative, comparing والله يعلم المفسد من المصلح.
NAHHAS:v3p61/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء يجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب مثل ﴿ والله يعلم المفسد من المصلح ﴾

NAHHAS:v3p61/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p61/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p61/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq rejects the accusative because an interrogative cannot be governed by what precedes; the question asks whether they or their opponents follow the path.
NAHHAS:v3p61/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق وهذا خطأ لأن الاستفهام لا يعمل فيه ما قبله ومن ههنا استفهام لأن المعنى فستعلمون أأصحاب الصراط نحن أم أنتم

NAHHAS:v3p61/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p61/r7.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري
NAHHAS:v3p61/r7.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read السوى on the faʿlā pattern without hamza, a rare feminine form of الصراط.
NAHHAS:v3p61/r7.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري ( فستعلمون من أصحاب الصراط السوى ) على فعلى بغير همز

NAHHAS:v3p61/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p61/r8.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v3p61/r8.claim: Abū Ḥātim rejects السوى: if derived from سوء it should be السوءى, and if from سواء it should be السيى.
NAHHAS:v3p61/r8.anchor: وقد رد هذا أبو حاتم فقال إن كان من السوء وجب أن يكون السوءى وإن كان من السواء وجب أن يقول السيى

NAHHAS:v3p61/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p61/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p61/r9.claim: Abū Jaʿfar defends the reading as arising from السوءى, with the quiescent hamza not a strong barrier before substitution by alif.
NAHHAS:v3p61/r9.anchor: قال أبو جعفر جواز قراءة يحيى بن يعمر والجحدري أن يكون الأصل السوءى والساكن ليس بحاجز حصين

NAHHAS:v3p61/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p61/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p61/r10.claim: ومن اهتدى is coordinated with the first من.
NAHHAS:v3p61/r10.anchor: ( ومن اهتدى ) معطوف على من الأولى

NAHHAS:v3p61/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p61/r11.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p61/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the first question as asking who did not stray, and the second as who strayed and then found guidance.
NAHHAS:v3p61/r11.anchor: والفراء يذهب إلى أن معنى من أصحاب الصراط السوي من لم يضل وإلى أن معنى ومن اهتدى من ضل ثم اهتدى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r1.claim: A skilled imitator may be described as a learner who follows a predecessor accurately, so a craft comes to be called that predecessor’s work.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r1.anchor: صنعة فلان وعمل فلان ووضعته في بعض موضع المتعلم الذكى والمقتدي المصيب في إقتدائه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r2.claim: Analogy across different kinds succeeds only when it finds a sound, intelligible resemblance and a genuine path of fit despite their visible differences; forced likeness produces awkwardness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r2.anchor: أن تصيب بين المختلفين في الجنس وفي ظاهر الأمر شبها صحيحا معقولا وتجد للملائمة والتأليف السوى بينهما مذهبا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r3.claim: Using a simile marker or borrowing a word does not itself make a true comparison; the writer must show a resemblance the imagination can actually grasp.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r3.anchor: إنما تكون مشبها بالحقيقة بأن ترى الشبه وتبينه ولا يمكنك بيان ما لا يكون وتمثيل ما لا تتمثله الأوهام والظنون

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r4.claim: Hidden similarities already have a rational basis; the critic earns praise by finding them through difficult thought, like discovering a pearl rather than creating its value.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r4.anchor: هناك مشابهات خفية بدق المسلك إليها فإذا تغلغل فكرك فأدركها فقد استحققت الفضل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r5.claim: A composite ornament or object requires parts whose forms and proportions fit; arbitrary substitute pieces cannot produce the same design, just as no impossible resemblance can be forced.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p130/r5.anchor: فإنما استحققت الأجرة على الغوص وإخراج الدر لا أن الدر كان بك واكتسى شرفة من جهتك

TABRISI:20:131/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:131/r9.claim: The phrase is governed by فستعلمون; من اهتدى has the same subject-and-predicate construction.
TABRISI:20:131/r9.anchor: ومن أصحاب الصراط السوي تعلق بقوله { فستعلمون } وهو مبتدأ وخبر وكذلك من اهتدى

TABRISI:20:132-135/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:132-135/r18.claim: Each side is waiting: the believers await God’s promise concerning the disbelievers, while the disbelievers await misfortune for the believers.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r18.anchor: أي كل واحد منا ومنكم منتظر فنحن ننتظر وعد الله لنا فيكم وأنتم تتربصون بنا الدوائر

TABRISI:20:132-135/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:132-135/r19.claim: The command “wait, then” is a threat.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r19.anchor: { فتربصوا } أنتم أي انتظروا وهذا على وجه التهديد

TABRISI:20:132-135/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:132-135/r20.claim: The sound path is the upright religion; the question asks whether the believers or their opponents are rightly guided.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r20.anchor: أي أهل الدين المستقيم { ومن اهتدى } إلى طريق الحق أي أنحن أم أنتم

DURR-FULL:v5p613/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r8.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the straight path as justice.
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r8.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {أصحاب الصراط السوي} قال: العدل

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r41.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r41.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r41.claim: Each side waits to see who will prevail; they are told to wait until God's command and the Resurrection arrive.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r41.anchor: قل يا محمد لهم كل متربص منتظر الدوائر ولمن يكون الفتح والنصر فتربصوا أنتم انتظروا فستعلمون إذا جاء أمر الله وقامت القيامة

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r42.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r42.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r42.claim: Another explanation is that each side waits for the other's destruction.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r42.anchor: وقيل: كل متربص هلاك صاحبه، وقيل: نحن نتربص وعد الله

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r43.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r43.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r43.claim: A further view says believers await God's promise coming to the disbelievers, while they await the believers' deaths.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r43.anchor: وقيل: نحن نتربص وعد الله ليأتيكم وأنتم تتربصون موتنا

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r44.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r44.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r44.claim: The outcome will show which side follows the straight road and true religion and is rightly guided.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r44.anchor: فستعلمون من] أصحاب الصراط الطريق السوي المستقيم والدين الحق ومن اهتدى إلى رشده نحن أم أنتم.

JISHUMI:v7p4774/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r4.claim: The ending of these verses conveys a severe threat.
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r4.anchor: ويدل آخر الآيات على وعيد عظيم.
